references.title: Google Street View actual Bernhardinkatu4 north annex, August2024; six pale framed windows, red brick and stone plinth actually opened at headings139 and176

observations: The publicly visible northern annex is one storey of red-brown exposed brick above a rough grey stone plinth, not a generic multistorey apartment facade.
Exactly six tall pale framed windows appear on this street front: four separated eastern windows and two grouped nearer the western church gate. Upper transom and vertical divisions are visible.

Brick pilasters, shallow segmental window heads, a corbelled brick frieze, projecting corner caps and a dark metal cornice are observed; this original chart represents their colour/line cues without adding geometry.
The street gate is west of this selected wall and is not painted as a doorway in the building. Native small recesses and stepped upper profile remain literal.

Nine exact native visual/HCOL street samples rise3.6610 to4.7021m over19.748m. Only the stone plinth follows these floor samples. Original horizontal windows use a separately declared datum5.8m below the highest native wall cap; dimensions are appearance approximations, not a physical survey.
The pale window frame is almost rectangular; the shallow segmental brick head is represented by brick courses, not a large pale arched hood.
limitations: Only13 exact facets on the three selected native northern support planes are authored. Other sides/courts and the separate German church VTJ103046323X remain unqualified.
Car foreground partly hides the lowest plinth; use uniform observed stone finish without copying vehicles or inventing basement openings.
Opening and brick module dimensions are approximate within the unchanged measured source wall, not an architectural survey. No reference pixels reproduced.
